THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:11367  MFA No. 102131 of 2016  JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the claimants in LAC No.57/2011 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Jamkhandi.
The appellants' land bearing Survey No.159/1 of Gadyal village, Tq: Jamkhandi,
was the subject matter of the Land Acquisition in terms of notification dated 14.02.2008 issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act 1894.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer has passed an award fixing Rs.63,115/- per acre as the market value for the wet land and Rs.35,075/- per acre is fixed as the market value for the dry land.
Being not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, the appellants sought reference in LAC No.57/2011.
The reference petition is allowed in part.
The compensation is enhanced to Rs.2,84,800/- treating the land as irrigated land.
Again the land loser is not satisfied with the award.
Hence, he is before this Court seeking enhancement.

Sri. N. L. Batakurki, learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that the land being the wet land, the compensation of Rs.2,84,800/- per acre awarded by Reference Court is on the lower side.
3. He would submit that the Co-ordinate bench of this Court in MFA No.103502/2017 has fixed Rs.10,15,000/- per acre as the market value of the land, for similar land.

He would submit that in the aforementioned case, the property under acquisition was a wet land, where the maize was grown and he would further submit that in the aforementioned case, the property was acquired in the year 2006.
It is also submitted that the property was also from the same village where the land of the present appellants is situated.
4. The learned counsel for the respondents would submit that the compensation awarded by the reference Court is just and proper and there is no scope for enhancing the compensation.

However,
it is also submitted NC: 2023:KHC-D:11367 by the learned counsel for respondents that the order passed in MFA No.103502/2017 is accepted by the State and no appeal is filed against the said judgment and award passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

sentences.text:
The point for consideration is "whether the market value fixed in MFA No.103502/2017 referred to above can be taken as basis to determine the market value of the land belonging to the appellants acquired under the notification dated 14.02.2008?"
6.
On perusal of the record, it is apparent that the land involved in the present case and the land involved in MFA No.103502/2017 were acquired under the notification of the year 2006.
It is also not in dispute that both the lands are acquired for the same project and the lands are from the same village and same taluk.
7. In this case, the Reference Court has given a finding that the land acquired is a wet land.
This finding is not questioned by the State.
Thus, there is no difficulty in holding that the land in question is a wet land.
The record of right produced by the appellants would also reveal that the appellants have grown maize.

In MFA No.103502/2017, this Court has fixed the compensation of Rs.10,15,000/- per acre,
in respect of the land where the maize was grown at the time of acquisition.
9. This being the factual position, this Court finds that the appellants have made out a case for enhancement of compensation.

Since the land belonging to the appellants is a wet land, where maize was grown and the notification was issued in the year 2006 to acquire the land, the appellant is also entitled to same compensation of Rs.10,15,000/- per acre as awarded in MFA No.103502/2017.
10.
For the aforementioned reason, the judgment and award passed by the Reference Court are modified.
The appellants are entitled to Rs.10,15,000/- per acre as compensation with all the consequential benefits.
It is further noticed that there was a delay in filing the appeal.
This Court vide order dated 16.04.2021 condoned the delay subject to the condition that the appellants are not entitled to interest for the delayed period, in case the compensation is enhanced.
Hence, the appellants are not entitled to interest for the delayed period of 1088 days in respect of the enhanced compensation.
12. It is brought to the notice of this Court that the appellants had claimed of Rs.4,27,000/- per acre as the compensation and accordingly, he had paid the court fee on the said amount.

Since,
compensation is enhanced, the appellants are required to pay the Court fee on Rs.10,15,000/-, on the enhanced compensation as contemplated above.

13. It is noticed that in MFA No.103502/2017, Co- ordinate Bench of this Court has awarded Rs.10,15,000/- per acre as the market value of the land in respect of the land situated in Gadyal village, Taluk, Jamakhandi and in NC: 2023:KHC-D:11367 the said case, the notification was issued in the year 2006.

However, it is to be noticed in this case, the notification is of the year 2008 and the Hasimpeer S/O Rajasab Mulla vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77533238/

sentences.text: 3 land is acquired for the same project.
Though the village is different, the taluk is same in both the cases and it is also noticed that the Reference Court has given a finding that the land is wet land.
The record of right produced by the appellants would indicate that the appellants were growing maize and sunflower.

Considering the fact that the land was acquired two years later than the land involved in MFA No.103502/2017, this Court is of the view that despite the villages are different,
since taluk is one and the same, this Court also is of the view that Rs.10,15,000/- per acre is to be awarded as compensation.
14. Appeal is allowed with proportionate cost.
15. Registry to draw a decree only on payment of the Court fee.
